title: Paradox Shoal
message: You step onto a tiny shoal floating among the stars... then step off it and somehow arrive on the opposite side of the exact same shoal. You try another direction. Same result. Again. Same result. Eventually you notice {reward} Star Candies sitting in the middle the entire time. Apparently leaving was optional.

title: Upside-Down Tidepool
message: A chunk of Moonlit Reef floats high above you, complete with glowing coral and a tidepool whose water refuses to fall. Tiny reef creatures swim overhead like this is perfectly normal. A few glowing droplets drift upward and expose {reward} Star Candies caught among the inverted coral.

title: Portal Roulette
message: Five portals shimmer in a suspiciously neat circle. The first moves you ten feet to the left. The second flips you upside down. The third drops you ankle-deep into Moonlit Reef water before immediately spitting you back out. The fourth somehow gives you a fake mustache. The fifth finally reveals {reward} Star Candies. Dozens of tally marks nearby suggest somebody tested these portals way more than necessary.

title: Walking Constellation
message: A tiny constellation detaches from the stars and begins following you. You stop—it stops. You move left—it moves left. You spin around—it spins around. Eventually it darts away, only to return moments later and excitedly circle {reward} Star Candies. Congratulations. Space has apparently adopted you.

title: The Infinite Slide
message: An impossibly long glowing slope disappears through several portals. There is absolutely no sensible reason to slide down it. Scratched beside the entrance are two words: "DO IT." Three portals, one sideways gravity shift, and an extremely undignified landing later, you crash beside {reward} Star Candies. Another message is scratched nearby: "Worth it."

title: Starfall Window
message: A rectangular tear in reality opens onto Starfall Trench. On the other side, celestial debris is falling upward. One tiny star fragment slips through, stops dead in front of you, and begins glowing like it suddenly forgot what gravity is. Its light reveals {reward} Star Candies nearby before the strange window quietly folds shut.

title: The Very Important Rock
message: An ordinary rock sits on a pedestal while stars orbit it, cosmic light shines upon it, and reality bends dramatically around its edges. Someone drew a tiny face on the stone. Beneath it: "His name is Gerald." Gerald is sitting beside {reward} Star Candies. You decide not to question Gerald.

title: Gravity Choir
message: A deep musical note echoes through the chamber and gravity pulls you firmly toward the floor. A higher note sends you sideways. Another sticks you to the ceiling. Then an even higher note launches you in a direction you are fairly certain should not exist. Scratched into the wall: "THE HIGH NOTE IS A LIAR." After several extremely graceful attempts, you reach {reward} Star Candies.

title: Kelp That Shouldn't Be Here
message: A strand of Whispering Kelp pokes through a tiny portal and slowly turns toward you. Another appears. Then another. All three lean closer as if inspecting you. You reach out—and every single strand immediately retreats through the portal. A few seconds later, one cautiously peeks back out. Their sudden retreat leaves {reward} Star Candies behind.

title: Duplicate Footsteps
message: Footsteps begin echoing behind you, perfectly matching your movements—except they happen about two seconds before you move. You stop. They already stopped. You turn left. They already turned. Eventually the footsteps wander somewhere you weren't planning to go. Against your better judgment, you follow them and discover {reward} Star Candies waiting ahead.

title: Hall of Other Selves
message: Endless mirrors show increasingly strange versions of you: a royal you, a ridiculously heroic you, a version carrying far too many Berries, and one wearing an enormous fake mustache. Most copy your movements perfectly. One turns around before you do. ...Nope. You investigate a much friendlier mirror instead and discover {reward} Star Candies hidden behind it.

title: The Berry Incident
message: Dozens of Berries float perfectly motionless in zero gravity. Nearby, someone has written: "I HAVE A PLAN." Farther in: "Okay." There is no explanation of the plan, what happened to it, or why so many Berries are now suspended in space. You decide ignorance is probably safer and retrieve {reward} Star Candies from the middle of the Berry field.

title: Leviathan Through Three Worlds
message: One colossal Leviathan bone stretches through three portals at once. One section is covered in Moonlit Reef organisms. Another hangs among Starfall debris. The third disappears into a place you don't recognize at all. Tiny creatures have built homes where the three realities intersect, and among their strange little settlement you discover {reward} Star Candies.

title: Yesterday's Campsite
message: You find a tiny campsite. Blink—it looks centuries old. Blink again—it looks freshly abandoned. Again—there is no campsite at all. Again—it's back. In one version you spot a Berry container, makeshift bedding, and a familiar doodled star beside the words: "Sleeping here was a terrible idea." Another flicker leaves {reward} Star Candies behind.

title: Memory Reef
message: Coral made from shimmering memories grows around you. One branch becomes Moonlit Reef water. Another flashes with Starfall starlight. Whispering Kelp winds through Leviathan bone while a Sunken Kingdom lantern flickers nearby. Then a memory briefly shows a familiar white-haired elf sprinting past with an armful of Star Candies. Before you can look closer, the memory shatters into light and leaves {reward} Star Candies behind.

title: The Door Argument
message: Two magical doors stand side by side. The first announces, "I AM THE ENTRANCE." The second immediately replies, "INCORRECT." They begin arguing. Someone has written nearby: "I picked the third one." There are only two doors. You turn around—and a third door is suddenly behind you. Naturally, it contains {reward} Star Candies.

title: Nexus Rain
message: Tiny stars begin falling around you like rain. Just before touching anything, each one dissolves into a harmless glowing droplet. Soon the entire Nexus sparkles with soft starlight. For once, nothing explodes, moves sideways, argues with you, or sends you through a portal. When the rain finally fades, the remaining lights gather around {reward} Star Candies.

title: Second Location
message: An entire merchant stall from Sunken King's Throne is sitting in the middle of the stars for absolutely no reason. The old merchant statue behind the counter is wearing a fake mustache. A crooked handmade sign reads: "SECOND LOCATION." The shelves are still empty. Business apparently has not improved. Beneath the counter, however, you discover {reward} Star Candies.

title: Gravity Garden
message: A beautiful garden grows in every direction at once. Flowers bloom from the floor, walls, ceiling, floating stones, and several surfaces you can't actually see. A trail of glowing petals gently rotates gravity as you follow it, letting you walk sideways, upside down, and eventually somewhere resembling normal again. At the end of the path bloom {reward} Star Candies.

title: The Helpful Portal
message: You spot {reward} Star Candies sitting only a few steps away. Easy. You approach—and a tiny portal moves them farther away. You approach again. Portal. Again. Portal. Again. Portal. Eventually the portal seems to get tired of its own joke, opens directly above you, and drops the Candies into reach. Scratched nearby: "IT DID THIS TO ME TOO."

title: First-Light Memory
message: The chaos of the Nexus suddenly disappears. No portals. No impossible gravity. No strange echoes. Instead, the Astral Sea stretches peacefully before you beneath a brilliant sunrise. Someone once sat here long enough to leave a shallow resting place and a tiny star scratched into the stone. Beside it rest {reward} Star Candies. After a quiet moment, the sunrise gently folds away.

title: Constellation Playground
message: A field of stars responds to everything you do. Jump—they jump. Spin—they spin. Wave—they wave back. Nearby tally marks lead to a sequence of notes: "Okay ONE more." Then: "Actually one more." Then: "LAST ONE." Much farther away: "...one more." Eventually the stars arrange themselves into an arrow pointing toward {reward} Star Candies.

title: The Room That Forgot You
message: You enter a perfectly ordinary room. You look away. Everything resets. Move a chair, turn around, and the room resets again—but the chair stays moved. Apparently the room forgets you, not the things you touch. After an embarrassing amount of furniture rearranging, you accidentally construct a path straight to {reward} Star Candies.

title: Wrong-Way Map
message: You uncover a hand-drawn map of the Nexus covered in increasingly desperate arrows. "THIS WAY!" becomes "WRONG WAY." Then "ACTUALLY THIS WAY." Then simply "HOW." Farther down: "I HAVE BEEN HERE THREE TIMES." And finally: "WHY IS THIS ROOM BACK." The map is almost completely useless—except for one tiny mark accurately pointing toward {reward} Star Candies.

title: Echoes of the Festival
message: Distant music drifts through the stars. Royal lanterns flicker into existence, followed by pieces of festival stalls and glowing decorations from Sunken King's Throne. For a few moments, part of the old King's Festival overlaps with the Nexus. One magical game booth lights up, declares you a winner without explaining the rules, and spits out {reward} Star Candies before the entire festival fades away.

title: Gnawed Timeline
message: Something is wrong with time here. You take a step—and suddenly you've taken three. A falling stone disappears halfway down and reappears already resting on the ground. A star simply loses several seconds of its own existence. It almost looks as though something has taken bites out of the timeline. One missing moment abruptly snaps back into place, bringing {reward} Star Candies with it.

title: The Shizuki Problem
message: The Nexus suddenly begins replaying old magical afterimages of a familiar white-haired elf. One Shizuki runs left. Another runs right. One points upward. Another appears to argue furiously with a portal. One sits down. One confidently marches in a direction every other echo immediately ignores. None of this is helpful. Finally, one last afterimage points toward {reward} Star Candies, gives an enthusiastic thumbs-up, and vanishes.

title: Astral Sea in a Bottle
message: An enormous glass-like sphere floats silently in the Nexus. Inside are tiny moving representations of Moonlit Reef, Starfall Trench, Whispering Kelp Forest, Leviathan's Wake, Sunken King's Throne, and the Astral Nexus itself. Currents connect the six mapped regions like a miniature living world. A small opening appears in the sphere and releases {reward} Star Candies into your hands.

title: Path Beyond the Map
message: Several currents stretch outward from the Nexus. Most carry familiar signs of the regions you've already explored. One does not. It flows away from every known path and continues beyond the mapped edge of the Nexus. You follow it with your eyes until it fades into distant starlight. An unfinished navigation mark nearby offers no explanation. The strange current leaves {reward} Star Candies behind before disappearing.

title: Heart of the Astral Sea
message:
The Nexus grows strangely calm. Around you, pieces of the entire known Astral Sea settle into place without fighting one another. Moonlit Reef water drifts upward through the air. Starfall debris hangs motionless among tiny stars. Whispering Kelp winds around a colossal Leviathan bone. Lanterns and festival decorations from Sunken King's Throne glow softly nearby, while Astral Nexus portals and constellations weave everything together.

Scattered through it all are little things you've learned to recognize by now: a doodled star, an old arrow, an empty Berry container, a tiny fake mustache, a scratched warning, and a familiar place where somebody once sat to rest.

An old Travel Note rests nearby.

"Made it this far, huh?"
"Pretty weird place."
"I like it."
"Still think there's more out there."

The Nexus answers with light. Moonlit Reef, Starfall Trench, Whispering Kelp Forest, Leviathan's Wake, Sunken King's Throne, and Astral Nexus flare around you like pieces of one enormous living map.

The light gathers and leaves behind {reward} Star Candies.

LEGENDARY EXPEDITION!

Then, just as everything begins to settle, another current appears beyond the six familiar paths.

It doesn't lead anywhere on the map.

Near its edge, scratched into the stone:

"Okay... this part isn't on my map."

The current stretches beyond sight.

Far away, something glimmers.

There is more to the Astral Sea.
